newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania exports to Japan decline in dollar value.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania exports to Japan decline in dollar value.

text.p: Tanzanian exports to Japan shrank in dollar terms by about 10 percent during the first six months of this year compared to the same period last year, a Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) official said.
The Jetro official said on Tuesday that Tanzanian earnings totalled $28.079 million (16.86 billion shillings) compared to $31.448 million (18.864 billion shillings).
The official said that when converted to yen, the earnings represented an increase of 4.6 percent, attributable to currency fluctuations between the dollar and yen.

Coffee is Tanzania's biggest export to Japan, earning $18.344 million (11.01 billion shillings) followed ny sesame seeds at $2.814 million (1.7 billion shillings), fresh water Nile Perch fish at $2.094 million (834.60 million shillings) and semi-precious stones at $544,784 (326,870 million shillings).
Japanese exports to Tanzania over the same period (January-June 1996) totalled $37.91062 million, the Jetro official said.
The Jetro official provided the trade figures in both dollar and Tanzanian shillings terms.
